issues.description: The problem specification (UML and textual description) declares SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() with return type void, but the reference solution implements checkOrderReady() as public boolean checkOrderReady(). This is a signature mismatch for a core API method and can confuse students about the expected method contract and return value.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent: either update the problem statement to specify checkOrderReady() returns boolean (and document the meaning of the return value), or change the solution (and any tests) so checkOrderReady() has a void return type and performs the same serving behavior without returning a value. Preferably modify the solution signature to public void checkOrderReady() to match the UML/spec, removing the boolean return and keeping the same side-effect behavior.
